idiom_name: typed Transducer/Reducer aliases over reduce and iterators, or @thi.ng/transducers
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the types that make the pattern safe: type Reducer<A, B> = readonly [() => B, (acc: B) => B, (acc: B, x: A) => B] and type Transducer<A, B> = (rf: Reducer<B, B>) => Reducer<A, B> catch element-type mismatches at compile time - exactly what is lost in C and in untyped JavaScript. @thi.ng/transducers implements the same idea at scale (~170 composable transducers and reducers, comp for left-to-right composition, transduce/reduce/iterator execution, reducers as 3-tuples of functions) and covers ES6 iterators plus async iterables through the companion package; without a library, Array.prototype.reduce, generator functions and iterator-helper chains express the same pipelines with types inferred by the compiler. What replaces the classic structure: generic function and tuple types plus inference replace the hand-rolled protocol, but at runtime the mechanism is identical to JavaScript - the classic structure is still justified when the transducer is published as library API surface, not merely used internally.
pitfalls: The transducer type cannot be expressed exactly: the rank-2 shape (a reducer generic in its accumulator) collapses to any in practice, so a wrong stage order still compiles unless every element type is written out.
Hand-rolled reducer tuples lose accumulator inference - the init function of a generic reducer cannot infer B from use - so stored pipelines need explicit annotations or the library's own types.
Types are erased at runtime, so the JavaScript traps (one-shot stateful transducers, single-use iterators, deferred-execution re-runs) are not caught by the compiler.
